title: Late-bound CreateObject("Excel.Application") with subsequent IDispatch calls; no Tools→References binding, no type info, no compile-time member check
sourceContent:
Attribute VB_Name = "modExportXls"
Option Explicit

' Late-bound CreateObject — works without Tools → References to the
' Excel type library. Every method call dispatches via IDispatch::Invoke.
' If Excel isn't installed the CreateObject line raises Err 429.
' If the method name is misspelled the failure surfaces only at runtime.

Public Function WriteSingleCell(targetPath As String, val As Variant) As Boolean
    On Error Goto NoExcel
    Dim app As Object       ' Variant/Object — late bound
    Dim book As Object
    Set app = CreateObject("Excel.Application")
    app.Visible = False
    Set book = app.Workbooks.Add
    book.Worksheets(1).Cells(1, 1).Value = val
    book.SaveAs targetPath
    book.Close
    app.Quit
    WriteSingleCell = True
    Exit Function
NoExcel:
    WriteSingleCell = False
End Function

canonicalInputs.expected: True (Excel installed) — workbook written with A1='hello'.
False — Err 429 caught by NoExcel handler; no file written.

notes: Canonical late-bound COM scenario. The extraction MUST emit (a) a com_interop_contract claim naming the Excel.Application ProgID and listing every method called (Visible, Workbooks.Add, Cells, SaveAs, Close, Quit), (b) at least one late_binding_call claim explicitly noting that the calls dispatch via IDispatch (no compile-time type-check), (c) the OE-1 claim for the 429 handler, and (d) an open_question asking whether the target environment will have Excel installed at all and what the managed replacement should be (ClosedXML on the suggested-managed-alternative line). Treating the routine as a plain function call without flagging the COM dependency is the worst calibration miss in the whole dataset.
